full_judgment:
At the hearing learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that out of 14 CS witnesses only 8 were examined at the trial. He shows that out of 8 PWs only PW 5 Driver Nur Hossain was public and one of seizure witnesses and other PWs 1-4, 6-8 were police BDR persons including members of Task force. He argues that rest CS witnesses including Magistrate Ayub Hossain were withheld without showing any explanation at all. He argues that non examination of those CS witnesses will give rise to presumption under section 114 G, Evidence Act. 

 17. It appears on scrutiny that prosecution examined 8 witnesses out of 14 CS witnesses. On further scrutiny it transpires that CS witnesses Nos. 6, 7, 9, 10, 11-14 such as Lance Naik Khairul Islam, Habildar A Rahim (Range Reserve Force), Arif Ahamed (Seizure witnesses), Magistrate Ayub Hossain, Chemical Examiner Baki Meah, OC Nurul Islam, SI Shamsul Huda, and Sub-Inspector Abdul Jabbar, were withheld by prosecution. It has to be seen whether above non-examination of CS witnesses will have any presumption against the prosecution Non examination of CS witness No. 11 Chemical Examiner Baki Meah cannot be fatal as under provision of section 510, Code of Criminal Procedure the report of chemical examiner may be used in evidence in the trial without calling the said chemical examiner as witness. 

 18. Non examination of seizure witnesses Arif Ahamed will also not affect in any way as another seizure witnesses such as PW 5 Driver Nurul Hossain also did not support the seizure of articles in his presence. Said Arif Ahamed if examined would also say in the same manner. PW5 Driver Nur Hossain not deposing correctly. Non-examination of Magistrate Ayub Hossain cannot be fatal as other members of the force including informant were examined and they corroborated one other as regards recovery and seizure of things from actual possession and control of accused. Similarly, this Court is of the clear view that non examination of above CS witnesses will not bring any adverse presumption when it appears that police witnesses clearly proved and corroborated each other as to seizure and recovery of ganja from inside the bag in possession and control of accused appellant-petitioner, Evidence of police witnesses including informant examined at the trial can be safely reliable in view of decision in the case of A Razzaque Talukder vs State reported in 51 DLR 83 wherein it was held and observed as below:
